options: "Of course, Dinoname is my friend!"
"I'll perform better if we've bonded."
"I'm doing chores. Unlike you, I don't mind hard work."
reply:
A

Sevene would say it plainly, "Of course Brutus is my friend!", because it's true, and six years of Ranger training have taught her that the bond with her dinosaur is a strength, not something to be ashamed of. Option B is a dodge, since she was singing to Brutus rather than doing chores, and C reduces their friendship to a tool for performance, which would quietly concede Orton's point. Owning the friendship without apology denies Orton the insecurity he's trying to stir up, and it shows a quiet confidence that matters more than courtly approval, especially from a girl of Bourg-les-Bains who chose a stable over Ermessen's table tonight.

options: Run to meet the guard, I have the sword in my favor.
Ask Aziz if there's a back way out of the monastery.
Ask Aziz if there's a place to hide.
reply:
C

Fighting the Royal Guard would turn men who may only be following orders into enemies, and might be exactly what Demorgon wants: me caught or bloodied before I ever reach the Outer Temple. Hiding just traps us more tightly in these walls. A back way out keeps Freya, Aziz and me alive and gives me the road to the temple, where I can decide in the open air, not with a blade at the door, whether to trust the gods, the monks, or the sword at my side.

options: "It's not your fault—it's my fault. I met someone who was looking for a room, and I told him about it. I'm so sorry."
"This is probably a good thing, I heard the neighbors have a rat problem." I'll lie to her so she doesn't blame me if she finds out I told Jace about the room.
"I thought you would've taken it by now. If you wanted it that badly, you should have gone for it."
"If you still want a place, I have a spare bedroom you can rent."
reply:
D

Salem is blaming herself for something I actually had a hand in, so the honest thing is to take my share: I knew she wanted the room and still sent Jace there. A lie like option A would protect me for a moment but poison her trust when she found out, and option B would pile more blame on someone already beating herself up. Owning it and apologizing gives our friendship its best chance, and once she's calmer we can talk about finding her another place.

options: I offer the standard message fee, same as I would to any urchin off the streets.
I turn my ally's vanity against them, offer something cheap but pretty.
I play upon our relationship, make a lot of the connection between us and its value.
reply:
A
An Aspect of Reality hungers for more than coin, and a pretty bauble would only teach Mirrors that I can be strung along. Our bond is real and worth more to both of us than any single message, so I'll remind them plainly: allies who squeeze each other at the hour of need soon find themselves without allies. It costs me nothing I'd regret, gives away no secrets, and keeps the one thread in this web I can still trust from fraying before the summit.

options: "I'm looking for a friend's bike."
"I was hoping you had some used bikes cheaper than the ones in the showroom."
"It's for a school project."
reply:
A

The truth is my best lever here. Hank already hates bike thieves enough to refuse kids, so telling him my best friend's bike was stolen and might have passed through his shop makes him an ally instead of a suspect-hunter. While he's checking today's bikes, I'll quietly put that ten-dollar bill back on his desk, because a detective who steals can't very well lecture anyone about thieves.

options: It'll be fine. I ripped up the ticket. Mrs. Claus was a bit annoyed, but Cai was grateful.
I told Cai I'd forget about the ticket if he taught me some magic tricks. He was reluctant, but went along.
I laid down the law. It improved my position at Claus Castle, but Cai is pretty ticked off.
I gave him the ticket but didn't push him on it. Claus was happy, and Cai was mildly grateful.
reply:
A
Fire codes keep people from burning, so the ticket should stand. A rule waived for a friend, or traded for magic tricks, would quietly turn me into a bribed official. But I don't need to grind Cai down either: once the rule has been applied fairly, a little grace keeps the door open to an ally I may need while the Heart is still missing.

options: "I just want to repair the Specular and go home."
"I'm going to return home a rich Man Woman."
"I'm repairing the Specular, but I'm not going home. I plan to remain here when this is all over."
"Stralchus may have built the Ziggurat, but he can't defeat the False Icon with it. I can. I plan to take his place."
reply:
D

Repairing the Specular keeps every door open, home included, without closing any for good. But after days of working alone I've drifted from the people here, and staying to help build something with them rather than over them (as B would) or off them (as C would) seems the truer aim. It also tells Therko plainly that I'm not after his place, which is the honest answer to the question he was really asking.

options: This means Heroname and Twinname are dead. Should I mourn?
Who is a part of whom now? This will take some getting used to.
I could get used to this.
I can't accept this. There must be a way of reversing the situation.
reply:
A

I can't mourn a sister whose memories are still breathing inside me, and I can't swear to undo something I don't understand yet, not while Clarissa is out there with the Matriarch. So I'll start with the honest question: who is a part of whom now? My hands remember a rapier and my voice remembers a teleprompter, and if I'm going to face Rebecca again, I need to know which of us is walking out of this hospital.

options: I'll talk to the people building the fire.
I know how to do it myself.
The physical fire is less important than the magic that goes into it. I'll focus on the magic.
reply:
C
A dozen counselors are already out there stacking wood, and after a day of trying to do everything my own way, I think I've learned that going it alone isn't working. If I talk with them, I can figure out how to make the fire burn hotter and longer, and maybe catch a stray thought or two about what people here actually know about the Timeless Circle. With Caitlin watching my every move, working openly alongside everyone else is also a lot less suspicious than slipping off to do something on my own.

options: Do something kind for him.
Threaten to push him into the pond. I care about my happiness, not his.
Tell a tale about the gods to explain why he should help me.
Discuss the tricks of worldly politicians to ease him into discussing the Star Ball.
reply:
C
I already spent one trick on the priestess, and when she finds the empty cup, word of a lying fox will spread through Hoshimori faster than I can run. A threat would only prove her right, and a clever speech is just another illusion. So I'll fetch the koi food he dropped, or stay and listen to his stories a while, and let him decide for himself whether this funny-looking furball is worth trusting with what he knows.

options: My careful and methodic investigation has given me the answer.
My charm and quick thinking have unraveled the truth.
My persistence and passion have revealed everything to me.
Thanks to my dogged determination, for once they'll have to believe me!
reply:
C

Before a hall of scholars, charm and passion only invite the charge that I've fooled myself, but a careful record of dates, depths, sightings and witnesses is something they can check for themselves. I'll open the journal, walk the Grand Royal Scholar through each entry, and invite the Society to repeat my route and test my findings. If the mermaids are real, the evidence will hold up under their scrutiny, and that will win them over far more surely than any rousing speech.

options: I've come prepared. I have a handheld electric shocker in my pocket, but it's been hastily put together.
I rush in and try my damnedest to draw the officers' attention away from Lewis.
I didn't come here to lose my life today. I retreat to a safe distance.
reply:
B

I brought these people here, and I won't watch Lewis get dragged off by his leg while I hide behind a lamppost. But an untested shocker against armed, angry police is how a brawl becomes a massacre, so I'll use my voice and my body instead: shouting, stumbling into their path, giving them a loud, unarmed white woman in a soaked skirt to deal with while the crowd pulls Lewis free. If I end up in a cell tonight, I'll wire Lamme the apology she's owed, but I'd rather miss the Fair than leave him to the gutter.

options: Loren needs to know what I saw.
I can't say anything, not until I'm certain.
There's no harm in asking if they've considered the possibility.
reply:
C

Loren is the one losing memories, and if Oriana is behind it, every hour I keep quiet is another hour she can take more from them, maybe even this conversation. I won't dress it up as certainty. I'll tell them exactly what I saw in the mirror room and admit I don't know what it means, so they can judge it with their own mind while it's still theirs. Hinting with a careful question would only be a way of hiding the truth from the one person in this house I trust.

options: Slash at its neck. It's a small target, but I think I can hit it.
Aim for the chest. That area already looks injured.
Didn't I hear about a draugr remedy that's used in the South?
reply:
A
The creature is weak and exposed now, and this is the moment to end it, not to stand searching my memory while it lunges again at my people. Every tale I have heard says a draugr is laid to rest by taking its head, and a leader who keeps her ground and strikes true when hard-pressed gives the scattered settlers a reason to come back. The neck is a small target, but the chest already holds spears and has not stopped it.

options: "It wasn't that bad, actually."
"That's right. They argued, and Justine tripped Sydney."
"Yes, but it wasn't my fault."
I don't say anything. I just wait for her to continue.
reply:
B

It's the plain truth: they argued and Justine tripped Sydney. Saying it straight keeps Ms. Martin's trust without handing her a secret she isn't ready to believe. Waiting in silence or saying "it wasn't my fault" would make me look evasive, and "it wasn't that bad" would downplay a fight my campers saw and will talk about. Being honest about what happened, and quiet about how, gives me time to find Justine and decide what Ms. Martin actually needs to know.

options: I used my personal prowess.
I formed my soldiers into a wedge, intent on bringing the swordfighters down as quickly as possible.
I used my magic to defeat Alliedlegion soldiers.
reply:
A

An officer's first duty in a riot is to turn a mob back into a unit, and a wedge does that: it pulls my soldiers out of the brawl and under my command again, and it drives straight at the men with live blades, who are the ones turning an insult into a massacre. Karakán asks for bravery *and* restraint, so I will not fling sorcery into a courtyard full of fleeing slaves, nor make a lone display of my own sword when men are dying. Let Kási Nirún see that the Storm of Fire answers insults with discipline. My captive for the god can be taken cleanly once the killing stops.

options: Threaten him.
Persuade him.
Bribe him.
reply:
B
He has already told me his price twice: "information can get a man killed" is a merchant naming the risk he wants paid for, and pleading a third time or revealing who I am would only draw eyes we cannot afford. A threat might loosen his tongue tonight but would bring the town's guards down on a thousand of my people tomorrow. A modest sum, enough to make his risk worth taking and with more promised once the captives are found, costs us some coin, but leaving our own in chains would cost us far more.

options: I'll tell her that I'm hungry—obviously that's why I came to the kitchens!
I'll ask her who's in charge, pretending that I'm angry. I want to get to the information right away and not waste time.
I'll ignore her.
reply:
B
A noble guest wandering in hungry is ordinary, a little embarrassing, and easy to forgive, so it calms her instead of frightening her. If I let her feed me and fuss over me, she'll chatter, and kitchen gossip about who gets trays carried to the east wing will tell me more than any demand would. Ignoring her or playing the angry lady would just make her remember me, and I can't afford to be remembered before dinner with Maki.

options: If I disable the sound system in the chamber, he won't be able to communicate with his followers.
If I tell him I know about his past, he might give up his quest for power, but I hope he doesn't recognize me in turn.
reply:
B
My ankle's shot, so talking my way out on a half-guess about his past is a gamble I can't afford, and it risks him working out who *I* am. That speaker system is the one thing in this room that doesn't fit a man who just wants company. If his hold on these people runs through those conduits, cutting it might wake up the neighbours I recognized, and they're the ones I came here to save, not fight.

options: "Where are these beings coming from?" I ask. "Where are they going?"
"You should know I answer more favorably to requests than to orders."
"You said you searched for friends. How can you know where they are?"
reply:
B

I'm about to carry someone down a treacherous slope toward a glowing front I know nothing about, while red rain burns the tail of the column behind us. Before I commit, I want to understand what this procession is and where it leads, both for her safety and for my own bearings in a realm that could swallow me whole. Asking also treats her as someone who knows this place better than I do, not as cargo or a commander.
